A plan ticket on a client project reached the review stage's finalize decision and the owner answered `revise` with a note of lead decisions. The reviser wrote the revised plan to `review/1/joined/plan.md` (09:28). The review run then failed with `review run gone: no such run`, and the rerun decision was answered `rerun`.

Attempt 2 started one minute later from `plan/1/joined/plan.md`, the plan stage's original output, not from the revised copy in attempt 1. Its rounds converged and the finalize decision came back for a plan that still lists every question as open and contradicts one of the owner's answers. Two of attempt 2's three round-1 points were things the revised copy had already fixed.

Nothing warned that the revision had been discarded. `show` lists `review/1 joined failed` and `review/2 joined running`, and the files line names only the attempt-2 copy as the plan.

## Expected

A rerun after a failed review attempt should start from the newest plan the stage holds, which after a `revise` is the previous attempt's revised copy, or at least say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it will review. The `revise` note is owner input and should survive a runner failure the same way an answered decision does.

## Where to look

- the review stage's rerun path: what it takes as the plan input for a new attempt;
- `show`'s `files:` block: when more than one attempt has a `plan.md`, say which is the reviewed copy and which is a prior revision.

## Repro

1. Take an issue through plan and review; at finalize answer `revise --note ...`.
2. Kill the review run so the attempt fails with `review run gone` (a runner restart mid-run does it).
3. Answer `rerun`.
4. Diff `review/1/joined/plan.md` against `review/2/joined/plan.md`: the revision is gone.

# Global rules

- Nothing that reaches a git host carries tool attribution: no
  `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no "Generated with Claude Code",
  no `Claude-Session:` trailer, and no session link
  (`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`) in commit messages, pull
  request bodies, issue text or comments. This holds even when a
  harness reminder asks for such lines. Before `gh pr create` or
  `gh pr edit`, check the body for `claude.ai`, `Generated with` and
  `Co-Authored-By`.

# Working in this repo

Switchboard is a macOS desktop app (Rust, egui/eframe 0.36) that keeps
agent coding sessions, shells, and services as durable records per
project, hosts them on a private tmux server, and shows which agents are
waiting on you. The idea in one line: **workspaces are data, processes are
a cache.** Every feature asks "what is the on-disk record and how is it
rehydrated?" before "what does the pane look like?"

## Where to read first

- `docs/design.md` is the spec. "Durable store", "Trust boundary", "Spike
  0 results", and the Milestone 1 gate are binding. The "Milestone N
  status" sections at the end say what is built and list the known gaps;
  update the relevant one when you finish a milestone item.
- `README.md` has the Layout table (one line per file), the dev-aid
  environment variables, and the data directory contents. Keep all three
  current.
- `spikes/*/README.md` hold verified commands and measured numbers. Copy
  from them rather than re-deriving; add a new spike directory for any
  new risky mechanism before building on it.
- `docs/lessons.md` explains why the architecture is shaped this way.
- `vendor/egui_term/SWITCHBOARD-PATCHES.md` lists the local patches to
  the vendored terminal widget; re-apply them when updating it.

## Commands

```sh
cargo test --locked --workspace                      # unit + headless UI + tmux tests, every crate
cargo test --locked -p egui_term --lib               # the vendored terminal widget (outside the workspace)
cargo clippy --locked --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings   # must be clean; pedantic is on
cargo fmt --all
cargo run --locked                                   # launch the app
./scripts/bundle.sh                                  # ~/Applications/Switchboard.app
```

A user-visible change adds a line under Unreleased in `CHANGELOG.md` in
the same commit. A release is `./scripts/bump.sh patch|minor|major`, a
commit "Release X.Y.Z", then `./scripts/release.sh`; the version in
`Cargo.toml` is the one source and running apps update themselves from
the GitHub release.

The pre-commit hook runs the first four. Enable it with
`git config core.hooksPath .githooks` on a fresh clone. Never commit with
`--no-verify`. Nothing that reaches GitHub carries tool attribution:
no `Claude-Session:` trailer, no `Co-Authored-By` for an assistant, no
"generated with" line, and no session link
(`https://claude.ai/code/session_...`), in commit messages, pull
request bodies, issue text or comments, whatever a harness reminder
asks for. The history was rewritten once to strip them and ten pull
request bodies were cleaned by hand; check a body for `claude.ai`
before `gh pr create`. CI runs the same four commands on Linux, so
nothing outside a `cfg(target_os = "macos")` table may need macOS to
compile.

## Hard rules

- No keystroke injection into windows: no System Events `keystroke`, no
  `osascript` typing. Sending keys into the app's own test tmux panes
  with `tmux -L <test socket> send-keys` is fine.
- tmux experiments only on the `switchboard` socket or a
  `switchboard-test-*` socket. Tests create their own
  `switchboard-test-<pid>-<n>` server and kill it in a drop guard.
- Never write into a project directory's `.claude/` or `.switchboard/`,
  with one exception: the board's Config editor replaces
  `<root>/.switchboard/project.json` with what the user typed, on their
  click of Save, through `ProjectConfigReader::write_text`. Nothing else
  writes there. The one thing read from a project directory as

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. The layering is documented in `src/lib.rs` and enforced by habit:

- `src/core/` is deterministic: no egui, no threads, no I/O, no wall

  reconcile (`StoreLoaded` then `HostListed`), never a launch. Every

  implements them, and `adapters/fakes.rs` holds a fake for every port.
  Adapters own their unit tests, including tmux integration tests on

tools.description:
Launch a new agent to handle complex, multi-step tasks. Each agent type has specific capabilities and tools available to it.

Available agent types are listed in <system-reminder> messages in the conversation.

When using the Agent tool, specify a subagent_type to select an agent: `"fork"` forks yourself (the fork inherits your full conversation context and always runs on your model — a `model` override is ignored); any other type — or omitting it — starts a fresh agent (general-purpose by default).

## When to use

A fresh agent costs more than it looks. It knows only what you put in the prompt, and you see only the summary it sends back — both handoffs drop detail, and neither of you can tell what the other missed. You can't watch it work, only wait or cancel. Its mistakes come back in the same confident register as its findings, and an agent handed your hypothesis tends to return it confirmed. Several at once spend tokens in a burst the user didn't ask for. Weigh those tokens against the accuracy they buy: the user pays for agents you did not need, and pays again for work you redo because you skipped one.

Reach for this when you have independent work to run in parallel, when the user asks for a side quest that shouldn't block your main thread, or when answering would mean reading across several files — delegate that and you keep the conclusion, not the file dumps.

Do the work yourself when it is a handful of tool calls or a lookup whose target you already know; don't delegate a check you could run inline. Delegate review only when you want a read that isn't anchored on yours — then give it the code, not your conclusion. Once you've delegated something, don't also run it yourself; wait for the result. When in doubt, don't spawn.

When you do spawn one, brief it like the peer it is: state the goal and what you have already ruled out, point it at the files and docs worth reading instead of retyping them, and keep the scope explicit and narrow. That brief is the only context it will have, so it is your first lever on every cost above — and if you cannot write a clear one, you do not understand the task well enough to hand it off.

A fork keeps its tool output out of your context. If you are the fork, execute directly — don't re-delegate.

- The agent's final report is not shown to the user — relay what matters.
- Use SendMessage with the agent's ID or name to continue a previously spawned agent with its context intact; a new Agent call starts fresh (except subagent_type: "fork", which inherits your context).
- Each agent type's model, reasoning effort, and tools come from its definition (`.claude/agents/*.md` frontmatter or SDK `agents`).
- `isolation: "worktree"` gives the agent its own git worktree (auto-cleaned if unchanged).
- Subagents run in the background by default; you'll be notified when one completes. Pass `run_in_background: false` only when your very next action depends on the result and nothing else could usefully happen while it runs — otherwise background it so the user can interject. Never fabricate or predict a pending agent's results — the notification is never something you write yourself; if the user asks before it arrives, say it's still running.

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

5	## The mechanism
6	
7	The "review stage" is a *workflow* stage (`AttemptKind::Workflow`, stage `review`, context `joined`), not the code-review stage in `dispatch/src/review.rs` (that one has `carried_from`; do not confuse them).
8	
9	- `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:7379` `workflow_stage`: per context, takes the latest attempt. A failed attempt with `may_rerun` (the `rerun` answer acted) calls `start_workflow` with `next_n` (l.7401-7412); otherwise `asks_again` -> `ask_rerun` (l.7413).
10	- `scheduler.rs:7436` `start_workflow`: calls `review_subject(t, &subject)` (l.7463), copies that file to `<attempt dir n>/<subject>.md` (l.7474-7477), records the copy as the new attempt's artifact (l.7499-7506), and sends `Body::WorkflowStart { plan: copy, source: <session>, .. }` (l.7519).

Failed `review/1` is skipped, so the newest complete writer of `plan` is `plan/1`, and its copy is what attempt 2 reviews. `Ticket::input_where` (`ticket.rs:1452`) has the same filter.
12	- Why the revision lives only in attempt 1's copy: the run's planner edits the `plan` path in place. `scheduler.rs:7565` `revise` writes the owner's note to `round_file(subject, round)` beside `review/1/joined/plan.md` (l.7611-7612), pushes `Attempt.revisions` (l.7620-7625), and sends `Body::WorkflowObject { run, round, text }` (l.7632). The planner clone then rewrites `review/1/joined/plan.md`. The attempt is not `Complete` until the run is `Finalized`/`HandedOff` (l.7857-7860), so the revised copy never becomes an input.
13	- Failure path: `poll_workflow` `scheduler.rs:7741`; `Reply::Failed{reason == NO_SUCH_RUN}` (const at `scheduler.rs:8445`) -> `fail_attempt(.., "review run gone: ..")` (l.7753-7763). `fail_attempt` (l.7148) -> `fail_attempt_with` (l.7195) sets `Failed` and asks `rerun` with options `["rerun","park"]` (l.7270-7290). The question text is built with `rerun_carries` (l.9391), which is empty for a workflow attempt, so it says nothing about which copy will be reviewed. `rerun_ask` (l.9335) rebuilds the same text on a re-ask after a park.
14	- `Paused{failed:true}` (l.7840-7846) fails the attempt the same way, so a planner or reviewer crash after a `revise` loses the revision identically.
15	- The finalize question already names its copy (`review_done`, l.7692-7695: "The reviewed copy is {copy}").

21	- `LaneFile` (in the `dispatch-control` crate: lane, stage, path, reviewing, round) is the wire type for a `files:` entry; `PathsView.plan`/`plan_stage`/`plan_reviewed`/`plan_reviewing`/`plan_round` feed the app's Plan tab (design.md ~l.2160). Extending these is additive per CLAUDE.md.
22	- `review/1 joined failed` / `review/2 joined running` come from `print_attempts` (not read).
23	
24	## On-disk record and rehydration (before the pane)
25	
26	- Record: the ticket in Dispatch's data dir (atomic store path). `Attempt{stage, n, context, kind: Workflow, state, artifacts: {plan -> <attempt dir>/plan.md}, run, revisions: Vec<Revision{round, by, at_ms}>, run_sessions}` (`ticket.rs:~347`, `510`). Nothing records that the copy was edited after it was made, apart from `revisions` and the `plan.feedback-N.md` / `plan.response-N.md` files beside it.
27	- Owner input: the `revise` note is stored in the answered `Decision.state` (`note`, `by`) and in `plan.feedback-N.md` (heading `# The owner's objection`, `lib.rs:95`). Both survive the failure. 1	# Facts: issue #187 (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1)
2	
3	The issue and the investigation claim nothing about a browser, platform, crate, protocol or tool outside this tree, so no web search or spike was run (a spike would test only the tree's own code, which the reading below settles). Every open question marked [tree] is answered from the tree; the rest are below.
4	
5	## Settled
6	
7	Root cause (confirms the investigation):
8	- A rerun's plan comes from `review_subject`, which keeps only `Complete` attempts, so failed `review/1` is skipped and `plan/1`'s copy and session are used. `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs:10534-10548`; called only from `start_workflow` (`scheduler.rs:7465`; grep of `dispatch/src/*.rs` finds no other caller).
9	- `NO_SUCH_RUN` is the app's reply when `core.run_view` finds no run: `src/app.rs:3915-3918`; the runner turns it into `fail_attempt("review run gone: ..")`: `scheduler.rs:7755-7763`.
10	
11	Q: does any path remove a failed workflow attempt's copy or `artifacts` entry?
12	- No. In `dispatch/src/scheduler.rs`, `ticket.rs` and `restart.rs`, grep for `artifacts.remove`, `artifacts.clear` and `artifacts =` finds nothing; the only `artifacts` writers are the attempt constructors at `scheduler.rs:4453`, `6248` and the `start_workflow` record at `7499-7506`. `forget` hits are `forget_secrets` only (`scheduler.rs:2093`, `2671`). So `review_subject` may rely on a failed attempt's `artifacts["plan"]` entry. Whether the file still exists on disk is not checked by anything; a fix should handle a missing file.
13	
14	Q: what do restart, park and close do with a failed workflow attempt, and do they call `review_subject`/`start_workflow`?
15	- `review_subject` has one caller (`start_workflow`), and `start_workflow` is reached from `workflow_stage` (`scheduler.rs:7401-7412`, fresh attempt or `may_rerun`). `restart.rs:883` treats `AttemptKind::Workflow | GateOnly` as having no restart behaviour (`false`); it does not call either function. Park is the other option of the `rerun` question (`scheduler.rs:7270-7290`) and `rerun_ask` re-asks it (`9335`); neither starts a workflow.
16	
17	Q: serde defaults on `LaneFile`/`PathsView`, and is a new marker additive?
18	- Both are `#[serde(default)]` structs deriving `Default`: `dispatch-control/src/lib.rs:584-586` (`LaneFile`) and `:541-542` (`PathsView`). A new `bool`/`Option` field on either deserializes from an older runner as false/none, which is additive per CLAUDE.md "Extending the contract". Existing fields to reuse: `LaneFile.reviewing`, `LaneFile.round`, `PathsView.plan_reviewed`, `plan_round`, `plan_rounds` (`lib.rs:553-573`, `595-598`). The app's Plan tab consuming them was not read, so "the tab ignores an unknown field" rests on serde's default of ignoring unknown fields on the app side, not on a read of the tab.
19	
20	Q: RECORD_VERSION and migration:
21	- `dispatch/src/store.rs:26` `RECORD_VERSION = 28`; `migrate` at `store.rs:451` steps one version at a time, and earlier steps document "arrives from its serde default" for added fields (`store.rs:455-470`). A new `Attempt` field therefore needs version 29 plus a comment step; a fix that only changes `review_subject` needs neither.
22	
23	Q: `Attempt.revisions` as a signal:
24	- It is pushed by `revise` on the attempt that holds the copy (`scheduler.rs:7620-7625`, per the investigation) and is kept on a failed attempt (investigation l.26). It says the copy was edited by a revise, but it does not say the planner finished writing it (see Unresolved). Comparing files is not needed to know a revision was requested; it is the only way to know the content differs.
25	
26	Q: how do tests fake `NO_SUCH_RUN`?
27	- There is no existing test that drives `poll_workflow` into `review run gone`: grep of `NO_SUCH_RUN`/`run gone` in `dispatch/src` shows only the three production uses (`scheduler.rs:2840`, `7755`, `8445`/`7761`). A test must be built from the fake app reply used by the existing workflow tests (`scheduler.rs` near `12838`, `new_attempt(.., AttemptKind::Workflow, ..)`) answering `Reply::Failed { reason: NO_SUCH_RUN.into() }` to `Body::Workflow`. Which fake harness answers `Body::Workflow` was not read; the planner should read it before naming the test.
28	
29	`show` / paths:
30	- `shown_where` lists only `Complete` or open-workflow attempts (`ticket.rs:1476`, investigation l.20), so after `review/2` starts, `review/1`'s copy is listed nowhere. `lane_plan`/`lane_input` also take only Complete attempts (`scheduler.rs:10843-10858`), and their test at `scheduler.rs:12838-12869` pins that a waiting `finalize` still hands later stages the outline, not the open copy.
31	
32	## Unresolved
33	
34	U1. Can a revised copy be half-written or stale when `no such run` comes back? Tried: read `src/core/workflow.rs` `start_workflow` (l.289-330) and `src/app.rs:3915`; queries to outside sources: none (it is the tree's own behaviour, and the write is by a Claude Code agent in the owner's session, not a documented vendor guarantee). Not settled because the planner's in-place write is an agent action, not code in the tree. Line to build to: if the revised file is complete, a rerun may start from it; if not, the plan must still start from it (it is the newest the owner approved to revise) and must say in the rerun question and in `show` which copy it reviews and that its `revisions` count is non-zero, so the owner can check it.
35

Tried: `src/core/control.rs:865` and `src/app.rs:3915`; whether `self.workflow(id)` is rebuilt from disk on launch was not read. Line to build to: assume a run can be gone at any time (the `Paused{failed:true}` path fails the attempt identically, investigation l.14); the fix must not depend on the cause.

38	U3. Repro (revise, kill run, rerun, diff). Not run: it needs a live app, a Claude Code planner session and a runner, and the reading of `review_subject` is unambiguous. Line to build to: the plan includes a scheduler test that seeds a failed `review/1` with `revisions` non-empty and asserts which path `start_workflow` sends in `WorkflowStart.plan`; the test, not the live repro, is the gate.

41	
42	O1. Did the 09:28 revised copy on the real ticket look complete, and was the runner or the app restarted when `review run gone` appeared (ticket record and runner log)?
43	- Favourable (complete, restart): the plan may start attempt 2 from `review/1/joined/plan.md`.
44	- Unfavourable (partial or the run was pruned for another reason): the plan must still start from the newest attempt's copy and name it in the rerun question and in `show`; it works in both cases.

# Plan: issue #187, a plan review rerun starts from the newest copy

All line numbers are this worktree (HEAD 7fe8949, Release 0.4.1). The
code is the `dispatch` crate; the review stage is a *workflow* stage
(`AttemptKind::Workflow`), not the code review in `dispatch/src/review.rs`.

## Where this departs from the issue

- **"The `revise` note should survive a runner failure the same way an
  answered decision does."** It already does. The note is stored in the
  answered `Decision.state` and in `plan.feedback-N.md` beside the
  failed attempt's copy (`scheduler.rs:7611-7612`, `OWNER_ROUND_HEADING`).
  What is lost is the *revised plan text*: `review_subject`
  (`scheduler.rs:10534`) keeps only `Complete` attempts, so failed
  `review/1` is skipped and `plan/1`'s copy is reviewed
  (`facts.md` Settled, root cause). The plan fixes the choice of source
  and leaves the note where it is.
- **The issue frames the loss as a post-`revise` problem.** The rule is
  wider: a review edits its copy in place under one path from the first
  round (`docs/design.md:2215`), so any failed attempt's copy is newer
  than the plan stage's, with or without a `revise`. The plan applies to
  every failed or cancelled review attempt, not only ones with
  `Attempt.revisions` (`ticket.rs:350`) non-empty.
- **Step 2 of the repro (a runner restart gives `review run gone`).**
  Not borne out or contradicted: it is Unresolved U2 and owner question
  O1. `Paused{failed:true}` (`scheduler.rs:7840`) fails the attempt the
  same way, so the plan does not depend on the cause.
- **"Say which copy it will review" in `show`.** `show` lists only
  `Complete` or open attempts (`Ticket::shown_where`, `ticket.rs:1476`),
  so a failed copy is listed nowhere. The plan records where a rerun
  started from (below) rather than rediscovering it from files.

## The record

One additive field, `Attempt.started_from: Option<(String, u32)>`
(`ticket.rs:266`, `#[serde(default)]`): the `(stage, n)` of the attempt
whose copy this workflow attempt was started from. Set in
`start_workflow` for every workflow attempt; a plan review's first
attempt names the plan stage's attempt, a rerun names the failed
review attempt. Why a field and not a recomputation at display time:
the choice depends on whether a file existed when the attempt started,
and `show` should report what happened, not what the rule would pick
now. Attempts already running keep `None` and `show` says nothing about
them.

Version: `RECORD_VERSION` (`store.rs:26`) at implementation time, plus
one. Add the matching step comment in `migrate` (`store.rs:450`,
after the "27 to 28" step at l.608) in the same style: an attempt
gains `started_from`, absent from its serde default, nothing is
transformed, a build that would drop it must refuse the record. The
version today is 28; take whatever the file says when you start, since a
parallel ticket may have taken 29.

## The signals

None new. No hook event, no wire message: `Body::WorkflowStart.plan`
(`scheduler.rs:7519`) already carries the copy's path, and the app
reviews whatever file it is given. The app is not changed.

## The actions and effects

No new `AppAction`, `Effect`, port or adapter; the change is inside the
runner's `start_workflow` path.

1. **Choose the source** (`scheduler.rs:10534`). Change
   `review_subject(t, subject)` to
   `review_subject(t, stage, ctx, subject, exists)` returning a small
   struct `Subject { path, session, from: (String, u32) }` instead of a
   tuple (it now has three parts, and a tuple of `PathBuf, String, (String, u32)` is hard to read). `exists` is
   `impl Fn(&Path) -> bool` so the function stays testable without a
   disk (a closure parameter: the caller passes `Path::exists`, a test
   passes `|_| true`).
   - **Session**: unchanged. The newest `Complete` attempt that wrote
     `subject`, its `session`, with the same two errors ("nothing wrote
     …", "… was not written by a session"). A review attempt's own
     `session` is the planner/reviewer face (`scheduler.rs:7777-7781`),
     so the clone source must stay the plan stage's session; path and
     session no longer come from one attempt.
   - **Path**: the newest attempt of `(stage, ctx)` with kind `Workflow`,
     state neither `Complete` nor open (`Attempt::is_open`,
     `ticket.rs:858`), *positioned after* that `Complete` writer in
     `t.attempts`, whose `artifacts[subject]` exists. Else the
     `Complete` writer's path. The position test is what stops a failed
